meta.title: Launching AI in Cobalt Ledger
meta.subtitle: Discussion document for the CEO
meta.purpose: Decide whether to launch an AI package for small-business customers now
meta.confidentiality: Fictional company; every number from public sources

storyline.governing_thought: Cobalt Ledger should launch its AI package now, built into bookkeeping and the month-end close, to win the small firms that have not yet adopted AI

exec_summary.text: Small firms are the next wave of AI adoption, and accounting is the function they have barely touched

sub_points.text: The share of US firms using AI rose from 17% to 25% between November 2025 and October 2026
Firms with 1–4 employees use AI at 56% of the rate of firms with 250 or more
In finance and accounting, 5.9% of the smallest firms use AI, compared with 20.5% of the largest

exec_summary.text: Small firms hold back because they cannot see where AI fits, not because of price, so AI has to come inside the tools they already use

sub_points.text: Among the smallest firms with no AI plans, 63% say AI does not apply to their business, while only 7% say it is too expensive
Small firms planning to adopt struggle most to find tools that fit (54%), and users worry most about accuracy (46%)

exec_summary.text: AI pays off in accounting and the leading platforms have already shipped it, so we should launch now, starting with bookkeeping and the monthly close

sub_points.text: Firms using AI accounting software closed their books 7.5 days faster, and accountants gave 55% more client support each week
Intuit, Xero and Shopify all launched AI assistants for small businesses between 2023 and 2025
Four moves: start with the close, turn AI on by default, show sources for approval, launch with the smallest customers

next_steps.action: Approve the launch budget and the H1 2027 launch date
Scope the package around bank-feed categorization and the month-end close
Design source-and-approve controls for every AI entry
Pilot with a group of our smallest customers and measure close time before and after

sections.title: Small firms are the next wave

lead_message.text: Our customers will soon expect AI: its use among US firms rose from 17% to 25% in under a year

slides.rationale: Changed over time, many points -> line-trend
slides.unit_line: **US firms using AI in any business function**, % of firms, last reading of each month, Nov 2025 to Oct 2026

sidebar.header: Adoption is building month after month, not spiking
sidebar.caption: relative rise in the share of firms using AI in eleven months
bullets: **Nov–Feb:** flat through the winter, before the climb began
**Mar–Oct:** up in almost every month, a steady climb rather than a spike
**For us:** customers meet AI in the other tools they use every day, and will look for it in ours

footnotes: Census reworded the question in November 2025 ("in any of its business functions"), so earlier readings are not comparable and are left out
The latest cycle (published Nov 5, 2026) renamed AI "Super Intelligence" in the question, and "Do not know" answers jumped; it is left out until the series settles

lead_message.text: Small firms use AI at about half the rate of large ones, leaving most of our customers still to adopt

slides.rationale: A is lower than B across size classes -> bar-ranking, kept in size order
slides.unit_line: **US firms using AI in any business function**, % of firms, by number of employees, Oct 2026

sidebar.header: Below 20 employees, adoption is flat; above it, it climbs with size
bullets: **1–19 employees:** all three classes sit at or below the national rate, and this is where our customers are
**Mid-sized firms:** the rate climbs with each size class
**Largest firms:** the highest rate, so the gap is about size, not about whether AI is useful

rows.label: Smallest firms' AI-use rate as a share of the largest firms' rate

footnotes: Census BTOS cycle 202621, reference period Sep 21 to Oct 4, 2026; employer firms only

lead_message.text: Under 6% of the smallest firms use AI in accounting, against over 20% of the largest — our core is open

slides.rationale: Same exhibit as the page before, one function (A-10) -> bar-ranking
slides.unit_line: **US firms using AI in finance and accounting**, % of firms, by number of employees, last six months, Nov 2025 to Jan 2026

sidebar.header: Our core workflow is where small firms lag the most
sidebar.caption: the largest firms' rate of AI use in finance and accounting, as a multiple of the smallest firms'
bullets: **Smallest firms:** the lowest rate of any size class, below the all-firm rate for this function
**Largest firms:** the highest rate, so AI in accounting already works at scale
**For us:** a ledger with AI built in brings small firms what large finance teams already use

series.name: Firms using AI in finance and accounting

footnotes: Census BTOS 2026 AI supplement; reference period November 2025 to January 2026

lead_message.text: Our job is to show small firms where AI fits, since cost is rarely what holds them back

slides.unit_line: **Reasons for not planning to use AI**, % of firms with 1–4 employees and no AI plans, Nov 2025 to Jan 2026

sidebar.header: The barrier is relevance, which product design can fix
bullets: **Not applicable:** owners do not see AI in their own work, so showing it inside the ledger answers this directly
**Lack of knowledge:** the second reason is also about not seeing the use, not about the technology
**Too expensive:** last of the six, so a price cut alone would not move these firms

rows.label: "Not applicable" answers for every "too expensive" answer

footnotes: Firms could choose more than one reason; shown are the six most-cited reasons other than "Other"

lead_message.text: Our package must be built in and checkable: adopters cannot find tools that fit, and users doubt accuracy

slides.rationale: Two clauses, one claim -> multi-chart-panel, no arrow (B-09)

panels.header: Before adopting, the hardest part is finding a tool that fits the business
panels.unit_line: **Top challenges, small employer firms planning to use AI**, % of firms, 2025

panels.header: After adopting, the worry is whether the answers are right
panels.unit_line: **Top challenges, small employer firms using AI**, % of firms, 2025

slides.so_what: Built-in AI ends the search for a tool; a source on every suggestion answers the accuracy worry
footnotes: Federal Reserve Banks' Small Business Credit Survey of employer firms with 1–499 employees, fielded September to November 2025

lead_message.text: Accountants using AI closed the books 7.5 days faster, the gain our customers would feel first

slides.rationale: Three results of one study -> kpi-big-numbers
slides.unit_line: **Measured effect of AI accounting software**, field data from small and mid-sized firms, 2025

items.caption: days faster monthly close
items.relation: The gain an owner sees at every close
drivers: General ledger entries also became 12% more granular
A shorter close puts cash and profit figures in front of the owner sooner
Measured on real transactions, not in a lab

items.caption: more weekly client support
items.relation: Time saved went to clients, not to cuts
drivers: Accountants answered more client questions each week
Time saved went to clients rather than to cuts in staff
For our customers: faster answers from their bookkeeper

items.caption: of accountant time moved from data entry
items.relation: Routine entry is where AI takes over first
drivers: Time moved to client communication and quality checks
Routine entry is the work AI took over first
So our first AI features should take on entry and categorization

footnotes: Field data from 79 small and mid-sized firms using one AI accounting product, plus a panel survey of 277 accountants; an observational study, not a randomized trial

lead_message.text: With Intuit, Xero and Shopify all shipping AI assistants to small businesses, waiting would leave us the exception

slides.rationale: Launches over time, with dates -> timeline-roadmap
slides.unit_line: **AI assistant launches by small-business software platforms**, by half-year, from company press releases
slides.so_what: AI is becoming standard in small-business software, so our risk is being late, not early
footnotes: Intuit: Sept 6, 2023 and July 1, 2025 press releases; Xero: Sept 3, 2025 media release; Shopify: Winter '26 Edition, Dec 10, 2025
Intuit says its agents save businesses up to 12 hours a month; Xero says 73% of its customers have used AI on its platform since March 2025

lead_message.text: Four launch moves turn this evidence into an AI package small firms will actually use

slides.unit_line: **AI package launch**, moves and the evidence behind each

items.text: Start with bank-feed categorization and the month-end close, where AI saves the most time
items.metric: days faster monthly close with AI (p. 8)

items.text: Turn AI on by default inside the screens customers already use, so they see where it fits
items.metric: of the smallest non-adopters say AI does not apply (p. 6)

items.text: Show the source of every AI entry and let the owner approve it with one click
items.metric: of small-firm AI users cite accuracy (p. 7)

items.text: Launch first with our smallest customers, where AI in accounting is least used
items.metric: of the smallest firms use AI in finance and accounting (p. 5)

slides.so_what: Decision today: approve the package for launch in H1 2027, starting with the monthly close
